memos.headline: JPM and XOM Near 52-Week Highs Lead Relative Strength; PG and UNH in Structural Downtrends
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe heading into year-end. JPM at 327.91 sits just 0.4% off its 52-week high with +5.0% 4-week relative strength vs SPY and RSI 63.6 — this is a textbook trend-continuation setup, and I'd stay long above the 50-day mean (~309). XOM is similarly positioned at only 0.6% off its high with positive relative strength across all timeframes. On the other side, PG is in a persistent downtrend — trading 7.5% below its 200-day mean, down 17.9% from its high, and showing -8.8% 12-week relative strength vs SPY — I see no reason to step in front of that. UNH's 44.6% drawdown from its 52-week high is extraordinary and while it has stabilized near the 50-day mean, the stock remains 5.7% below its 200-day with negative relative strength, so I'd wait for a confirmed trend reversal above the 200-day before getting involved. CAT's 12-week +21.3% return and +18.0% relative strength are impressive, but at 35.2% above the 200-day mean I'm cautious about chasing the extension — a pullback toward the 50-day would be a better entry.

views.note: Just 0.4% off 52-week high with strong 4-week relative strength of +5.0% vs SPY and RSI 63.6; would reassess on a close below 309.
Only 0.6% off 52-week high, above both moving averages with positive relative strength across timeframes; invalidated below 116.
Persistent downtrend with price 7.5% below 200-day mean, -17.9% drawdown, and -8.8% 12-week relative strength vs SPY — no sign of a bottom.
Despite stabilization near the 50-day, the 44.6% drawdown and -5.7% vs 200-day mean signal structural damage; need a reclaim of the 200-day to reconsider.
Strong +9.4% weekly bounce with +4.1% 4-week relative strength and RSI 58.7, but 12-week relative strength is slightly negative; would cut below 175.
Flat near the 50-day mean with RSI 50.1 and -9.4% 12-week relative strength vs SPY — no edge either way until it reclaims 500 or breaks 470.
Extraordinary 26-week +89.8% run leaves it 45.8% above the 200-day mean, creating mean-reversion risk despite only a 3.1% drawdown; too extended to chase.
Impressive 12-week +21.3% return but 35.2% above the 200-day mean is stretched; prefer to buy a pullback toward the 50-day rather than chase here.
Sitting right at the 50-day mean with RSI 49.1 and negative 4-week relative strength of -3.1%; need a push above 280 for conviction.
Orderly uptrend above both averages but 8.5% drawdown and flat 4-week relative strength suggest consolidation rather than breakout.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Lead on Earnings Power; UNH Margin Collapse Warrants Caution
memos.body: I see the strongest durable earnings power in NVDA and GOOGL this cycle. NVDA posted $57B in quarterly revenue (+62.5% YoY) with a 56% net margin and only $8.5B in total debt—extraordinary operating leverage that I want to own. GOOGL delivered $102B in revenue (+15.9% YoY) at a 34.2% net margin with minimal leverage ($14.8B debt), showing disciplined cost management alongside healthy top-line growth. On the other end, UNH's net margin collapsed to 2.1% with net income down 61.2% YoY despite 12.2% revenue growth, signaling severe cost or reserve pressures that I cannot underwrite at current levels. XOM's revenue declined 5.2% YoY with net income falling 12.3%, and an 8.8% net margin leaves little cushion if commodity prices soften further—I'd need to see stabilization before getting constructive.

views.note: 62.5% YoY revenue growth, 56% net margin, and only $8.5B total debt represent best-in-class earnings power; a sustained margin decline below 45% would change my view.
15.9% revenue growth with a 34.2% net margin and low leverage ($14.8B debt) demonstrate durable, high-quality earnings; I'd reassess if ad revenue growth decelerates below 10%.
18.4% YoY revenue growth and a 35.7% net margin on $43.2B debt show strong cloud-driven earnings momentum, though net income growth of 12.5% lagging revenue growth bears monitoring.
Revenue of $180B (+13.4% YoY) with net margin expanding to 11.8% and net income up 38.2% signals improving profitability, but $55B in debt and still-thin margins keep my conviction moderate.
7.9% revenue growth and 26.8% net margin are solid but $90.7B in total debt is the highest in this universe ex-JPM; I need to see services mix accelerate to get more constructive.
31% net margin and 11.6% net income growth are respectable for a bank, but the rate cycle outlook and $427B debt load limit upside conviction.
Steady 21.2% net margin and 20% net income growth are reassuring, but only 3% top-line growth caps the earnings trajectory.
Revenue grew 9.5% YoY but net income fell 6.7%, compressing the margin to 13%; I need to see margin stabilization before turning constructive.
Net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to a 2.1% net margin on $80B of debt—this is cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for until margin recovery is visible.
Revenue down 5.2% and net income down 12.3% with an 8.8% net margin leave little buffer; I'd need commodity price stabilization and margin recovery above 10% to reconsider.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact but Labor Market Softening Warrants Caution on Cyclicals
memos.body: The Fed has cut 75bp over the past year, bringing the upper bound to 3.75%, while CPI is running at 2.7% YoY—still above target but trending in the right direction. I am concerned that unemployment has risen to 4.50%, up 30bp YoY and 20bp over just the last three months, signaling a labor market that is cooling faster than the headline easing cycle might suggest. The 10y-2y spread has steepened 38bp over the past year to +0.68pp, which is constructive for banks but also consistent with the market pricing in further easing amid slowing growth. The 10y yield at 4.14% has fallen 44bp YoY, providing a tailwind for duration-sensitive growth names, though I would be cautious on pure cyclicals given the labor deterioration. A January payrolls print showing unemployment at or above 4.7% would shift my regime call from 'late-cycle easing' to 'recession risk,' which would flip me defensive across the board.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from falling long rates and continued Fed easing; 10y down 44bp YoY supports multiples.
Lower rates support premium growth valuations, though consumer softening from rising unemployment is a modest headwind.
Steepening curve (+38bp YoY on 10y-2y) is positive for net interest margins, but rising unemployment could pressure credit quality.
Defensive staple positioning is warranted as unemployment trends higher; CPI at 2.7% supports pricing power without margin destruction.
Rising unemployment and late-cycle dynamics make pure cyclical exposure unattractive despite the easing backdrop.
Falling long-end rates favor high-duration growth; secular AI demand provides an offset to macro softening.
Energy lacks a clear macro catalyst; slowing growth is a demand headwind but easing policy provides some floor.
Defensive characteristics are appealing but healthcare is more idiosyncratic; macro signals are mixed for the sector.

memos.headline: Limited Sentiment Signal Across Universe; UNH and XOM Filing Clusters Warrant Monitoring
memos.body: I have very little GDELT-style media tone data to work with this cycle—my evidence set consists entirely of 8-K filings and two price reactions, with no direct media sentiment or tone scores. That said, filing frequency itself can proxy for narrative intensity. UNH stands out with three 8-Ks in a compressed window (Nov 7–21) covering Reg FD disclosure, bylaw amendments, and officer changes, suggesting elevated corporate activity that could attract negative media scrutiny. XOM filed five 8-Ks between Oct 31 and Dec 9, the highest volume in the universe, though its earnings-day price reaction was a muted -0.3%, implying the market has already digested the news flow. NVDA's Q3 results triggered a -3.2% next-day decline, a clear negative tone event, but that was over a month ago and likely priced by now. Without granular tone data I keep confidence low across the board and lean neutral on most names.

views.note: Unusually dense 8-K cluster including bylaw changes and officer departures suggests governance turbulence that may sustain negative media tone.
Five filings in six weeks is high volume but the negligible -0.3% earnings-day reaction suggests the narrative is already absorbed by the market.
The -3.2% post-earnings drop on Nov 19-20 was a clear negative tone event but is now five weeks stale and likely priced.
Three 8-Ks including a mid-December officer change are routine for a staples name; no tone shift signal detected.
Single director/officer change filing on Dec 5 is low-signal from a sentiment perspective.
Officer change and shareholder vote filing on Dec 8 is standard governance activity with no discernible tone shift.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Plunges 44% in One Month While WTI Slides Below $59—Geopolitical Tailwinds Favor Tech, Headwinds for Energy
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped sharply to 181.39, down 44% month-over-month, while VIX sits at a benign 13.47 (down 34% over the same period) and HY spreads have tightened 31bp in a month to 2.84%. This combination signals that near-term sanctions escalation, export-control surprises, or major trade-policy shocks are not being priced by markets heading into year-end. WTI crude at $58.72—down over 10% in three months—suggests either demand weakness or a perception that energy supply disruptions (Russia, Middle East) are contained, which is a structural negative for upstream producers like XOM. I have moderate conviction that the current calm is real for the next quarter but low conviction it persists beyond that; a renewed round of China semiconductor export controls or an OPEC+ supply cut reversal would change my view. For now, the de-risked policy backdrop favors large-cap tech names with diversified supply chains over energy and names with concentrated regulatory exposure.

views.note: Export-control risk to China AI chips remains structurally elevated even as near-term uncertainty has eased; any new Commerce Department rule would flip this to avoid.
Falling policy uncertainty and benign VIX support consumer-tech multiples; supply-chain diversification away from China reduces geopolitical tail risk versus prior years.
WTI at $58.72 and down 10% over three months reflects contained geopolitical supply risk; multiple 8-K filings suggest ongoing corporate adjustments but the macro energy backdrop is unfavorable.
Broad de-escalation in policy uncertainty and tight credit spreads support capex-heavy cloud and logistics buildout with limited near-term geopolitical headwinds.
Antitrust and regulatory overhang is idiosyncratic rather than geopolitical; benign macro-policy backdrop is supportive but I lack conviction on structural resolution of DOJ proceedings.
Low policy uncertainty and stable credit conditions favor defensive consumer staples with global supply chains; no adverse geopolitical signals in recent filings.
